title: Plan concurrent journey branches only with explicit fan-out, release, join and failure semantics

facts.note: Task text or plan draft mentions running journey branches or wagon operations concurrently.
Planner is authoring plan artifacts, including acceptances or docs that carry concurrency proof.

values: journey topology adds parallel branches or a join
facts.note: Needs a plan/journey-diff observer detecting fan-out/join edges, multiple incoming continuations treated as a join, within-wagon concurrency, or edits to concurrency evidence.

values: operations independent and expensive; measured saving exceeds concurrency overhead
facts.note: Independence and cost/benefit are judged from the plan and benchmark data.

fires: A planner proposes running two independent expensive journey operations in parallel to cut latency.
A journey draft routes several continuations into one step and treats it as a synchronization point.
A plan proposes fan-out/fan-in across interlockings.
A wagon plan introduces concurrency inside the wagon.

A planner edits acceptances or docs that prove (or omit) bounded concurrency, joining, cancellation, failures, result equivalence or latency for concurrent branches, even if branch structure is unchanged.
doesNotFire: A purely sequential journey with one outgoing continuation or terminal per route and no concurrency planned anywhere in it.
Editing journey wording unrelated to concurrency, joins or their evidence.

given: A plan introduces or changes concurrency: parallel journey branches or within-wagon concurrency, or its evidence
when: the planner authors the topology, wagons, acceptances or docs for it
then: Plan branches as concurrent only if the topology explicitly specifies fan-out, dependency release, join, and failure semantics; otherwise keep them sequential.
prefer: Concurrency only for independent expensive operations whose measured saving exceeds its overhead.
Prove bounded concurrency, prerequisite satisfaction, joining, cancellation, failures and result equivalence; benchmark latency.
avoid: Treating multiple incoming continuations as a join.
More than one outgoing continuation or terminal per route; assuming journeys give fork/join.
Inferring unimplemented orchestration or a new runtime dispatch option from this pattern.
why: Journeys allow one continuation or terminal per route and lack fork/join, so unspecified parallelism is unsynchronized and unverifiable. Within-wagon concurrency can honor existing contracts.
evidence: Proof of bounded concurrency, prerequisite satisfaction, joining, cancellation, failure handling and result equivalence.
A latency benchmark shows the measured saving exceeds concurrency overhead.
Topology names fan-out, dependency release, join and failure semantics explicitly; existing plan and source validators pass.
verifier_detail: Advisory guidance for agents (severity 3), not independent enforcement or a new runtime dispatch option; existing plan and source validators apply.

Flag journeys where a step with multiple incoming continuations is relied on as a join, routes with more than one outgoing continuation/terminal, and fan-out/fan-in spanning interlockings. Within-wagon concurrency is within the current runtime boundary (can honor existing contracts).
audit: Source term ids: applicability, constraints, evidence, runtime_boundary
